text:
sara: Quick check-in — proposing a phased refactor of the big session service into smaller encapsulated domains. High level: session-routing, kv-cache (bounded to session state), and affinity-controller. Goal is to reduce blast radius and make targeted paydown of tech debt. Thoughts?

raj: +1 to boundary clarity. how do we handle ownership of session metadata vs ephemeral cache?

sara: plan is: session-routing owns canonical session metadata (ttl, owner, route), kv-cache remains the fast local store (not canonical), affinity-controller owns placement/host affinity decisions. We'll introduce explicit read-through to canonical store for miss/consistency windows.

marta: do we have a migration pattern? rolling cutover or big bang?

sara: rolling. idea = announce dual-read for a few deploys, then flip writes, then prune old fields. fallback route always hits old monolith until canary metrics look good.

ben: what metrics will we gate on? latency p95, error rate, token-cost?

sara: p95 latency for hot paths (<20ms target), error rate <0.1% above baseline, and a small spike threshold on cross-service calls (<15% increase). Also instrument per-route cost so we can detect unexpected amplification.

leah: telemetry question — we need a schema for session events so downstream analytics don't break during dual-read. suggest a compatibility shim in events pipeline.

raj: data migration consistency — do we use background converger to patch old sessions to new domain form? any plan to ensure idempotence?

sara: yes, background converger that reads canonical session store and materializes necessary kv-cache keys. idempotent by design (compare-and-set on version). We'll ship converger as a separate job with throttling and backoff.

marta: ops runbook for rollback? can't have partial writes that leave sessions in unknown state.

sara: runbook: 1) flip writes back to monolith (feature flag), 2) switch router traffic to monolith fallback, 3) drain converger queue, 4) roll back deploys. We'll add a safety guard in affinity-controller to refuse placement if it sees inconsistent version header.

ben: curious about cost tradeoff — splitting increases RPCs in some flows. any modelling?

sara: early numbers: +10-12% RPCs on session start, but expected -30% tail latency on heavy-enrich calls because of smaller critical path. we can tune batching and local caching to offset RPC increase.

deploy-bot: deploy started: session-routing v2 -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

leah: small nit — can we add a short-lived compatibility field in event schema instead of dual payloads? reduces transform logic downstream.

sara: good call. we'll add event.compat_v2 and mark for cleanup in 90 days.

raj: one last ask — document explicit SLA changes for Dedicated customers when we split. some customers rely on the old single-host behavior.

sara: noted, i'll draft a customer impact note and attach to the RFC. planning a customer-facing cherrypick window for Dedicated tenants.

marta: sounds like a reasonable path. happy to own the canary and rollback playbook.

sara: thanks — i'll update the RFC with the converger sketch, runbook, and metrics. tagging @eng-sre for preflight. :white_check_mark:
